svg.title: Shared and private targets
svg.desc: A shared target is visible to and usable by everyone; its credentials can be updated by anyone signed in only if whoever created it allowed updates. A private target is visible to and usable only by the user who made it, anything built on it is private too, and by default its creator can update its credentials. Credentials are whatever the target is configured with and never decide visibility. Every target reports whether the provider rejected its credentials on the last request, and shows nothing until it is used.
svg.text: Who can use a target
Visibility and credential updates are chosen when the target is created. Neither depends on the credentials.
Shared (default)
Everyone sees it and can use it.
Configured on the server, or created in the
GUI or API with "Only me" off.
Credentials can be updated only if its creator
(or initializer) allowed it; then by anyone.
"private": false
"allow_credential_updates": false
Private ("Only me")
Only its creator sees it and can use it.
For anyone else it doesn't exist.
Anything built on it (a scorer, round robin,
technique) is private too.
Its creator can update its credentials.
"private": true
"allow_credential_updates": true
Credentials either way: whatever the target is configured with (a key, any headers, the server's
identity, or none). An update replaces the key or headers in place, without recreating the target.
Every target shows how the provider answered the last request: key = accepted, lock = rejected, nothing until it's used.
